BiCGSTAB (stabilized BiCG) for improved smooth convergence on nonsymmetric systems (Enhances BiCG by introducing a stabilization (minimal residual) step to reduce oscillatory behavior; widely used with ILU-type preconditioners.)

Cholesky (LL^T) factorization for SPD matrices (For SPD matrices A=LL^T (or A=R^TR), enabling fast solves and log-determinants; numerically stable and halves the floating-point work compared to LU for SPD problems. Forms the basis of many preconditioners.)

Gaussian/LU factorization specialized to band-diagonal matrices (Stores only the populated diagonals and performs band-aware elimination with reduced fill and operation count proportional to the bandwidth. Common in PDE discretizations where the bandwidth is modest relative to n.)

LU decomposition with (partial) pivoting for solving Ax=b and computing determinants (Factorizes a nonsingular matrix A into PA = LU with a permutation P, unit-lower L, and upper-triangular U. Once factored, multiple right-hand sides and determinants are efficient, and the factorization is more stable than naive Gauss-Jordan.)

Conjugate Gradient (CG) for sparse symmetric positive definite systems (Krylov subspace method minimizing the A-norm of the error; per-iteration cost is O(nnz) and convergence depends on κ(A) and preconditioning quality. Cornerstone solver for large SPD problems arising from PDEs.)

Generalized Minimal Residual (Builds an orthonormal Krylov basis via Arnoldi and chooses the iterate with minimal residual over the subspace; restarted and flexible variants control memory and cost. Robust and widely applicable with suitable preconditioning.)

Björck-Pereyra O(n^2) algorithm for solving Vandermonde systems (Exploits the special structure of Vandermonde matrices to reduce work and improve numerical behavior compared to naive Gaussian elimination; useful in polynomial interpolation contexts.)

Thomas algorithm (tridiagonal matrix algorithm) for O(n) solution of tridiagonal systems (Performs a forward sweep eliminating subdiagonal entries followed by back substitution, exploiting the tridiagonal pattern for linear-time work and storage. Stable for diagonally dominant or SPD problems; otherwise pivoting may be needed.)

Classical Gaussian elimination with pivoting plus back-substitution for dense linear systems (Forward elimination transforms A to an upper-triangular U using row operations and (usually) partial pivoting; back-substitution then solves Ux=b. This is the workhorse of dense linear algebra and forms the basis for LU factorization used by LAPACK and most libraries.)

Gauss-Jordan elimination to compute reduced row-echelon form and matrix inverses (Row-reduction with both forward elimination and full back-elimination to produce RREF and, optionally, A^{-1} by augmenting with the identity. Robust pivoting strategies are essential; numerical stability is generally inferior to LU with partial pivoting for solving Ax=b. This method is pedagogically transparent but rarely used in production solvers for dense systems.)

BiConjugate Gradient (BiCG) for nonsymmetric sparse linear systems (Extends CG to nonsymmetric matrices by building polynomial approximations in bi-orthogonal Krylov subspaces; may suffer irregular convergence, often superseded by stabilized variants like BiCGSTAB.)

Cyclic tridiagonal solver via Sherman-Morrison rank-1 update (Reduces a cyclic tridiagonal system to a standard tridiagonal solve plus a low-rank correction using the Sherman-Morrison formula; retains O(n) structure while handling periodic boundary conditions.)

Cholesky (LL^T) factorization for SPD matrices (For SPD matrices A=LL^T (or A=R^TR), enabling fast solves and log-determinants; numerically stable and halves the floating-point work compared to LU for SPD problems. Forms the basis of many preconditioners.)

Gaussian/LU factorization specialized to band-diagonal matrices (Stores only the populated diagonals and performs band-aware elimination with reduced fill and operation count proportional to the bandwidth. Common in PDE discretizations where the bandwidth is modest relative to n.)

LU decomposition with (partial) pivoting for solving Ax=b and computing determinants (Factorizes a nonsingular matrix A into PA = LU with a permutation P, unit-lower L, and upper-triangular U. Once factored, multiple right-hand sides and determinants are efficient, and the factorization is more stable than naive Gauss-Jordan.)

Thomas algorithm (tridiagonal matrix algorithm) for O(n) solution of tridiagonal systems (Performs a forward sweep eliminating subdiagonal entries followed by back substitution, exploiting the tridiagonal pattern for linear-time work and storage. Stable for diagonally dominant or SPD problems; otherwise pivoting may be needed.)

Iterative refinement (iterative improvement) to enhance solutions of direct factorizations (After solving Ax=b via a direct factorization, compute the residual r=b−Ax in higher precision, solve Ad=r, and correct x←x+d; repeat until convergence. Modern variants enable mixed-precision workflows that recover high-precision accuracy at the cost of a few refinement steps.)

A computational workflow applying Logical Data Analysis (LDA) to investigate destruction patterns among ancient Egyptian objects from the Cachette de Karnak. The workflow formalises observed destruction features as a binary context over 333 objects and uses the RAP (Rules and Patterns) algorithm, implemented in **OSCAR** via **Jupyter Notebook**, to extract a minimal implication basis from the data. The derived logical rules are evaluated for statistical and scientific relevance, testing whether damage distributions encode systematic, intentional destruction practice.\N\N### Main steps\N\N**Extract objects** — extract 333 relevant objects from the Cachette de Karnak database.\N\N**Define properties** — define discriminating properties for the subset.\N\N**Encode objects** — encode each object as a binary string per property.\N\N**Compute rules** — compute the Gröbner basis of the boolean ring to extract logical rules.\N\N**Interpret results** — evaluate the statistical and scientific relevance of the derived implications.
